items.root_cause: two-copies-of-a-rule, textbook. The gate's own comment (audit-match-soundness.ps1:178, 'A verdict names (commodity, store) but NOT the item') was TRUE when written: verdict files through 2026-07-30 carry no item field (352 of 407 entries recover no identity at all). Verdict files started carrying a structured item field on 2026-08-05, and the item-first refinement was then implemented INLINE in two consumers (verify-apply.ps1:60-64, purge-verdict-lows.ps1:247) without ever being hoisted into verdict-lib.ps1, the file whose header says it is THE one definition of item identity. The third consumer, the accept gate, kept identifying its subject by re-parsing rendered prose, and its founding premise silently disarmed. Consequences cut both ways: a reason quoting a flavour word false-blocks an innocent real product (garlic, and the same shape sits live on bacon and parmesan), and a quote capturing a size or a reordered name silently under-enforces a reviewed DROP (heavy-cream '169 fl oz', butter word-order).

root_fix.what: hoist the identity rule into the shared lib so there is exactly ONE definition: move verify-apply's Get-VerdictIdentity($entry) into verdict-lib.ps1 (item field first, Get-VerdictQuotedItem fallback, empty string when neither); make all three consumers call it (accept gate switches to it; verify-apply deletes its local copy; purge-verdict-lows.ps1:247 replaces its inline branch). verdict-lib stays param-less and pure ASCII per its own header.
root_fix.exact_change: verdict-lib.ps1 += function Get-VerdictIdentity($entry) { if ($entry.PSObject.Properties['item'] -and $entry.item) { return [string]$entry.item }; return (Get-VerdictQuotedItem ([string]$entry.reason)) }. verify-apply.ps1: delete lines 60-64 (the lib version loads at the existing dot-source on line 51; note the local definition currently shadows the lib AFTER dot-source, so deletion is required, not optional). purge-verdict-lows.ps1:247: $judged = Get-VerdictIdentity $e.
